description: Public-transport punctuality now in a German region: share of trips >5 min late, skipped stops, cancellations, trend, alerts in force. Use when asked if buses and trains run normally, a strike, storm or works disrupt them, or for a line with no place ("ist die RB33 pünktlich?" → line: answered where it runs, or asks which region). Do NOT use for a station's departures or a line from a named DEPARTURE station ("RE1 ab Köln Hbf?"; "nach …" is no station) — get_train_departures. Figures are region-wide. Window ≤ 120 min. CC BY-SA (DELFI) or CC BY 4.0 (VBB, Berlin/Brandenburg): show attribution.

language.description: Set this on every call to the language the person is writing in: "en" if they wrote English, "de" if they wrote German. Do not leave it out: it defaults to German ("de"), which is only the fallback when the language is genuinely unclear, so an English question sent without it is answered in German — a wrong answer. Place names, station names and road numbers are never translated in either language; in English the German term is kept in parentheses so the person recognises it on signs and in local apps.

lat.description: Latitude in WGS 84, e.g. 48.137. Use with lon when the caller already holds coordinates; otherwise use region.

line.description: A line name as on the vehicle, e.g. "RB33", "S1", "RE 1", "U6". Give it when the question names a line; with no region the answer covers the Kreise the line runs through, or names the regions where lines of that name run. With region, it is that region's line of the name.

lon.description: Longitude in WGS 84, e.g. 11.576. Use with lat; otherwise use region.

region.description: The German region to report on, as free text: a Bundesland ("Bayern", "Bavaria", "Nordrhein-Westfalen"), a city ("Hamburg", "Köln"), a Kreis ("Landkreis Fulda") or one of the conurbations Ruhrgebiet, Rhein-Ruhr and Rhein-Main. A town inside a Kreis is reported as that Kreis and the answer says so, because the data is filed at Kreis level. Not a stop, not a street, not an address. Give either region OR lat+lon, never both.

window_min.description: How many minutes back to look, 5–120 (default 60). The trend compares this window with the equally long one before it, so 60 means "the last hour against the hour before". Use a short window for "right now" and a long one for "has it been bad all morning".

name: check_transit_disruption
